why: Build the string one character at a time; you may add '(' while opens < n and ')' while closes < opens. That pruned decision tree is exactly the set of balanced strings, and trying '(' first emits them in lexicographic order.
hints: At any point while writing, which of the two characters are you still allowed to write without making the string unfixable?
Track counts of opens and closes. Add '(' if opens < n, add ')' if closes < opens. When length reaches 2n, record it.
Recursive DFS trying '(' before ')' gives ascending lexicographic order directly. Output size is the nth Catalan number (16796 for n = 10).
pitfalls: Try '(' before ')': since '(' < ')' in ASCII, that order produces the required sorted output.
Generating all 2^(2n) strings and filtering works for tiny n but is wasteful; prune instead.
